questions.q: Which Configure Start option enables an after-save flow?
options: Fast Field Updates
Set Entry Conditions
Actions and Related Records
A record is deleted
questions.explain: Actions and Related Records is the after-save option, chosen in the same Optimize the Flow For section as Fast Field Updates.

questions.q: What can an after-save flow do that a before-save flow cannot?
options: Read the triggering record's fields
Create new records and run Actions like sending an email
Run at all
Be given a Label and API Name
questions.explain: After-save flows can update any record, create new records, and run Actions — none of which before-save flows can do.

questions.q: In the Opportunity-to-Contract example, why must this flow run after-save?
options: Because creating a new, related Contract record is outside what a before-save flow is allowed to do
Because Contracts can only be created on a schedule
Because Opportunities don't support before-save flows at all
Because Create Records only works in screen flows
questions.explain: Creating a new related record is exactly the kind of action restricted to after-save flows.

questions.q: What does Debug let you do before activating a record-triggered flow?
options: Permanently delete the flow
Run the flow against a real record you choose, without affecting live automation
Automatically activate the flow for all users
Convert it into a before-save flow
questions.explain: Debug runs the flow's logic against a chosen record so you can verify its behavior safely before activating it.

questions.q: Per this lesson's rule of thumb, when must a record-triggered flow be after-save rather than before-save?
options: Whenever it only updates a field on the triggering record
Whenever it needs to touch a different record, create something new, or run an Action
Whenever the flow has fewer than three elements
Never — before-save can always be used instead
questions.explain: The moment a flow needs to touch another record, create a record, or run an Action, it must be after-save.
